slot.brief: A figure showing a Williamson synthesis setup — given R-X and R'-ONa, ask the student to pick the correct ether product and explain why the reverse pairing (halide from the hindered group) fails.

stem: In the Williamson synthesis shown in the figure, the major product is:

verdicts.working: The reactants are sodium tert-butoxide and bromoethane. In Williamson ether synthesis, tert-butoxide displaces bromide from the primary ethyl halide to give ethyl tert-butyl ether.

working:
Williamson ether synthesis proceeds via SN2. Ethyl bromide is a primary alkyl halide, which is good for SN2. Sodium tert-butoxide, although hindered, still acts as a nucleophile with the unhindered primary halide; the SN2 transition state is accessible, leading to ethyl tert-butyl ether. The alternative pairing (t-BuBr + EtONa) would largely undergo E2 elimination because tert-butyl halide is too hindered for SN2, so di-tert-butyl ether is not formed. Diethyl ether requires ethyl bromide and sodium ethoxide, which are not present. Methyl ethyl ether requires a methyl halide or methoxide, not present.

Independent check: The reactants are sodium tert-butoxide and bromoethane. In Williamson ether synthesis, tert-butoxide displaces bromide from the primary ethyl halide to give ethyl tert-butyl ether.
solution:
Williamson ether synthesis proceeds by $S_N2$ substitution. Bromoethane is a primary halide, so tert-butoxide displaces bromide to form the ether:
$$\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CONa + C_2H_5Br \rightarrow (CH_3)_3COC_2H_5 + NaBr}$$
The major product is ethyl tert-butyl ether.
